cornerCallouts: The Senna S, a crucial section to carry speed; a slight mistake here can cost valuable time.
Turn 4 is a tricky braking zone, especially with cold tires; expect to see some lock-ups there.
The long sweeping Turn 5, a real test of the car's balance and the driver's commitment.
The entry to Turn 7 is deceptively fast, requiring pinpoint accuracy to avoid running wide.
Turn 8 is a tight hairpin, a prime overtaking opportunity if you can get the car stopped.
The exit of Turn 9 is critical for setting up a good run down the back straight.
The final corner, Turn 10, demands precision and control as the drivers hustle to the finish line.
Drivers need to be wary of the walls through Turn 3 and Turn 4 – very little margin for error on this street circuit.
strategyPoints: Tire degradation will be a major factor on this abrasive surface, with the softest compounds likely to struggle over a long stint.
With a lap time of around one minute, the pit window opens up fairly early, but the undercut could be powerful.
Fuel consumption will be a key consideration, especially in the early stages of the race when the cars are running close together.
The tight confines of the circuit make overtaking difficult, so track position will be paramount.
A safety car is highly likely on a street circuit like this, potentially throwing a wrench into the established strategies.
The optimal pit stop strategy will likely be a one-stopper, but a two-stopper could be viable if the tire degradation is extreme.
The relatively short length of the circuit means that drivers will be lapping slower cars frequently, increasing the risk of incidents.
Managing the brakes will be crucial, especially in the braking zones for Turns 4 and 8, to avoid overheating.
weatherCommentary: The humidity here in Salvador is always a factor, making life difficult for the drivers inside the cockpit.
Rain showers are common in this region, and a sudden downpour could completely change the complexion of the race.
The sea breeze can also play a role, affecting the car's aerodynamic balance, particularly through the faster sections.
The track temperature can fluctuate wildly throughout the day, impacting tire performance and grip levels.
The tropical climate of Salvador means that the drivers will need to stay hydrated and manage their energy levels carefully.
